title: Batteries (Management and Handling) Rules, 2001 (as amended to 2010)
citation: S.O. 432(E), MoEF, 16 May 2001; amended by S.O. 1002(E), 4 May 2010
currency: SUPERSEDED. Replaced by the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 (S.O. 3984(E)), which the library now holds as battery_waste_rules_2022.

scope.applies_to: Manufacturers, importers, reconditioners, assemblers, dealers, recyclers, auctioneers, consumers and bulk consumers of lead acid batteries.

battery_definition.text: Lead acid battery which is a source of electrical energy and contains lead metal.

key_points.text: Bulk consumer: government departments, undertakings, boards and companies purchasing one hundred or more batteries per annum.
Manufacturers, importers, assemblers and reconditioners collect back used batteries against new sales, set up collection centres, and send them only to registered recyclers.
Dealers take back used batteries against new sales with a discount and transport them safely to designated collection centres or registered recyclers.
Consumers deposit used batteries only with the dealer, manufacturer, importer, assembler, registered recycler, reconditioner or designated collection centre.

routing_implications.summary: Lead acid batteries return through the dealer take-back chain, not municipal routes. Household 'waste batteries' are SWM special care waste (SWM r. 3(1)(zx)) and go to deposition centres.
